277	  records the normalized reservations (the field is omitted when they
278	  were not provided), and ``resume`` of such a checkpoint matches one
279	  uninterrupted call field by field; a checkpoint whose
280	  ``reservations`` is corrupt raises ``TypeError`` or ``ValueError``.
281	- ``replay`` re-checks a candidate path against the same reservations:
282	  a successful path verifies with the same ``cost`` and ``steps``.
283	  With ``diagnose=True`` a path entering a reserved vertex reports
284	  ``reservation_vertex`` and a path traversing a reserved edge in
285	  reverse reports ``reservation_edge``, each with the zero-based index
286	  of the first offending element; every other invalid path keeps the
287	  existing fixed structure and error codes.

289	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
290	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
291	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
292	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
293	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
294	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
295	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
296	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
297	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
298	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
299	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
300	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
301	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
302	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
303	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
304	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
305	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
306	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
307	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
308	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
309	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
310	  other arrival times still compete.
311	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
312	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
313	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
314	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
315	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
316	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
317	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
318	  better route with a worse one.
319	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
320	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
321	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
322	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
323	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
324	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
325	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
326	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
327	  and step count.

329	Top-k planning (``plan_k``):
330	- ``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
331	  dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None,
332	  allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` returns
333	  several distinct feasible routes on the same grid in one call. It
334	  first performs exactly ``plan``'s shared validation for the
335	  dimensions, coordinates, static obstacles, positive integer cost
336	  matrix and dynamic frames (including the frame-0 start check), and
337	  only then checks ``k``: a non-bool positive integer is required,
338	  wrong types raise ``TypeError`` and non-positive values raise
339	  ``ValueError``. The optional ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost``
340	  limits are checked after all of that (the ``k`` check included),
341	  still before the search starts, with the same non-negative,
342	  non-bool integer rules ``plan`` uses (other types raise
343	  ``TypeError``, negative values raise ``ValueError``). The optional
344	  ``dynamic_costs`` frames are validated after all of those checks,
345	  still before the search starts, with the shared time-varying cost
346	  rules (providing both ``costs`` and ``dynamic_costs`` raises
347	  ``ValueError``). Every error is
348	  decided before the search starts, and ``plan_k`` accepts no
349	  ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` argument.
350	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, the zero start cost, the
351	  entering-cell cost accumulation, the persistent last frame, the ban on
352	  waiting in place and on repeated coordinates, and the static/frame
353	  feasibility rules. Routes that reach the same cell through different
354	  coordinate histories are distinct candidates and are never merged, in
355	  both static and dynamic mode, so different complete coordinate
356	  sequences always remain separate results.
357	- It returns ``{"paths": [...], "costs": [...], "expanded": int}``: at
358	  most ``k`` unique complete routes ordered by ascending total cost and,
359	  on ties, by the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate
360	  sequence; ``costs`` corresponds to ``paths`` entry by entry. The first
361	  entry is the route ``plan`` would return. When no route is feasible
362	  both lists are empty and ``expanded`` still reports the route
363	  candidates actually closed to determine the answer: one count per
364	  complete history, and never counting a candidate filtered at
365	  generation or left pending. The traversal stops the moment the k-th
366	  goal route has been closed, so a small k closes strictly fewer
367	  candidates than a larger one. ``start == goal`` yields only the
368	  single-point zero-cost route, with one expansion. Every returned route
369	  verifies offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count, in
370	  both static and dynamic mode; the result never depends on obstacle-set
371	  iteration order, in-frame coordinate order or the traversal order.
372	- ``max_cost`` caps a route's accumulated entering-cell cost exactly as
373	  in ``plan``: the start still costs 0, a candidate exactly at the
374	  limit still competes and a candidate whose accumulated cost would
375	  exceed it is discarded the moment it is generated. It never changes
376	  the tie-break between legal routes. ``max_expanded`` caps the number
377	  of complete route candidates actually closed (exactly what
378	  ``expanded`` counts); once the limit is reached no further candidate
379	  is closed, and the limit only ever truncates the traversal -- it can
380	  never replace an already determined higher-ranked route. When either
381	  limit is provided the result additionally carries ``status``:
382	  ``"found"`` when all ``k`` routes were closed or the search exhausted
383	  naturally with at least one route; ``"budget_exhausted"`` when fewer
384	  than ``k`` routes were found and the budget stopped the search while
385	  candidates were still pending (this wins when both limits fire);
386	  ``"cost_exhausted"`` when fewer than ``k`` routes were found, no
387	  budget stop occurred and at least one candidate was discarded for the
388	  cost limit; ``"unreachable"`` when no route exists with neither a
389	  budget stop nor a cost discard. The routes already closed (and their
390	  costs, in rank order) are still returned when a limit ends the search
391	  early, as empty lists when none were found, and ``expanded`` is the
392	  actual closed count. Omitting both limits keeps every legacy key and
393	  value exactly unchanged.

396	- ``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None,

400	  one shared grid in a single call. It returns ``{"results": [...]}``

402	  order of ``requests``; duplicate requests are kept and each gets its

404	- The shared arguments are validated with ``plan``'s rules and order,
405	  with ``requests`` taking the position of ``start``/``goal`` in that

409	  two-element sequence ``[start, goal]`` of grid coordinates: element
410	  shape or coordinate type failures raise ``TypeError``; out-of-bounds

417	  with no state shared across queries. The optional ``dynamic_costs``
418	  frames follow the shared time-varying cost rules and are validated

420	  is then answered exactly as an independent ``plan`` call with the

422	  ``status``,

426	  directly. A successful path ends at its request's goal and verifies
427	  offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count. The result
428	  never depends on obstacle-set iteration order, in-frame coordinate
429	  order or the permutation of ``requests``.

431	Multi-start planning (``plan_multi_start``):
432	- ``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
433	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
434	  max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` plans from
435	  several candidate starts to one shared
436	  goal in a single call and returns one deterministic route, in exactly
437	  the result structure of ``plan``; the path begins at the winning start
438	  and ends at ``goal``. ``starts`` takes ``start``'s position in
439	  ``plan``'s validation sequence and every shared check keeps its order,
440	  exception type and message boundary.
441	- ``starts`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates: ``None``,
442	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
443	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each start follows the
444	  coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or coordinate types
445	  raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and starts on static
446	  obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated starts merge and the tuple is
447	  sorted, so the input ordering never changes any result. A start
448	  blocked by dynamic frame 0 raises ``ValueError``; every check runs
449	  before the search starts.
450	- In static mode every start is a ``g == 0`` root and each coordinate is
451	  closed at most once: a cell keeps only its best known ``(cost, path)``
452	  pair (smallest accumulated entering-cell cost, then the
453	  lexicographically smallest complete coordinate sequence -- an ordering
454	  preserved under common extensions, so a dominated candidate can never
455	  win later). In dynamic mode the persistent last frame, the ban on
456	  waiting and on repeated coordinates apply, and routes reaching the
457	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
458	  states that are never merged. Time-varying ``dynamic_costs`` frames
459	  (validated after every other check, before the search) make the
460	  search time-expanded the same way obstacle frames do: entering a
461	  coordinate at path index ``t`` costs that frame's cell value, the
462	  last frame persists, and the trace records ``(x, y, t)`` triples.
463	- The winning route has the smallest total ``cost``; ties are decided by
464	  the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate path, so the result
465	  never depends on the input order of ``starts``. Expansion order is f,
466	  then h, then ``(x, y)`` (plus ``t`` in dynamic mode), and finally the
467	  complete path. ``cost`` counts only the cells entered (the winning
468	  start costs 0); ``expanded`` counts only closed candidates; when no
469	  route exists ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``.
470	- With ``trace=True`` static mode records the unique coordinate closing
471	  sequence and dynamic mode the ``(x, y, t)`` closing sequence, and
472	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. A ``starts`` entry equal to
473	  ``goal`` yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same
474	  start-equals-goal and zero-budget rules as ``plan``.
475	- ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost`` follow ``plan``'s ``status`` and
476	  budget-priority rules: a candidate whose accumulated cost would
477	  exceed ``max_cost`` is discarded without counting toward ``expanded``,
478	  and neither limit ever changes the unlimited route or the tie-breaks.
479	  With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop returns a JSON-serializable
480	  checkpoint recording the sorted starts, the grid constraints, the
481	  dynamic frames, the time-varying cost frames when they were provided,
482	  the cost limit when one was provided and the complete
483	  pending state; ``resume`` continues it with the cumulative-budget,
484	  no-double-counting and only-budget-exhausted-snapshots rules of the
485	  other planners, and invalid checkpoints follow ``resume``'s usual
486	  ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` boundaries.
487	
488	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
489	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
490	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
491	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
492	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
493	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
494	  included) and before the search starts.
495	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
496	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
497	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
498	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
499	  carry the field.
500	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
501	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
502	  candidate goals, costs, dynamic frames and the cost limit when one was
503	  provided), the closed-node count, the
504	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
505	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
506	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
507	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
508	  back to ``resume`` later.
509	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
510	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
511	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
512	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
513	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
514	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
515	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
516	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
517	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
518	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
519	  closed node twice.
520	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
521	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
522	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
523	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
524	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
525	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
526	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
527	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
528	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
529	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
530	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
531	
532	Offline replay (``replay``):
533	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
534	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
535	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
536	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
537	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
538	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
539	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
540	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
541	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
542	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
543	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
544	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
545	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
546	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
547	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
548	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
549	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
550	  ``start == goal``.
551	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
552	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
553	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
554	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
555	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
556	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
557	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
558	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
559	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
560	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
561	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
562	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
563	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
564	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
565	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
566	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
567	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
568	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
569	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
570	  ever returned.
571	
572	Distance field (``distance_field``):
573	- ``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None,
574	  trace=False)`` is an offline analysis entry point for the static grid:
575	  it accepts only the dimensions, the static obstacles, a single goal and
576	  optionally ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no
577	  search budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option. The dimensions,
578	  goal coordinate, obstacle and costs checks (structure, integer types,
579	  bounds, duplicate merging, goal-on-obstacle) follow ``plan``'s public
580	  rules and order for those shared arguments and all run before the
581	  search starts; ``trace`` must be a bool (``TypeError`` otherwise).
582	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "expanded": int}`` where ``distances``
583	  is a height-by-width matrix indexed ``distances[y][x]``: ``None`` for
584	  obstacles and for cells that cannot reach the goal, ``0`` for the goal
585	  itself, and for every other reachable cell the minimum sum of the
586	  entering-cell costs along a four-neighborhood route from that cell to
587	  the goal (unit steps without ``costs``; with ``costs`` each move adds
588	  the cost of the cell entered, exactly as ``plan`` accumulates ``cost``,
589	  so a reachable ``plan`` start yields the same value ``plan`` reports
590	  as ``cost``). No reachable distance is ever negative and the matrix
591	  always matches the grid dimensions; the result is JSON-serializable.
592	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the reachable cells determined and closed
593	  once each, the goal included. The closing order is fully specified:
594	  smallest current distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate in
595	  lexicographic order, so neither the obstacle-set iteration order nor
596	  the costs layout traversal influences the matrix, the count or the
597	  trace. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally carries
598	  ``expanded_nodes``, the coordinate pairs in that closing order, and
599	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``; the field is omitted entirely
600	  when ``trace`` is false or omitted.

602	Multi-goal distance field (``distance_field_any``):
603	- ``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
604	  trace=False)`` is the multi-goal counterpart of ``distance_field``:
605	  one offline analysis returns the minimum-cost field to any of the
606	  candidate endpoints in a single pass. It accepts only the dimensions,
607	  the static obstacles, a non-empty ``goals`` sequence and optionally
608	  ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no search
609	  budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option, and it never produces a
610	  ``status`` field. The dimensions, obstacles, costs and trace checks
611	  follow ``distance_field``'s public rules and order, and ``goals`` is
612	  validated exactly like ``plan_any``'s: ``None``, strings, bytes and
613	  other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, an empty sequence raises
614	  ``ValueError``, elements that are not exactly two non-bool integers
615	  raise ``TypeError``, and out-of-bounds coordinates or endpoints on
616	  static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. The goals checks occupy
617	  ``goal``'s position in ``distance_field``'s validation sequence,
618	  duplicates merge, and every check runs before the search starts, so
619	  the input permutation never changes any result.
620	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "targets": ..., "expanded": int}``.
621	  ``distances`` is the same height-by-width matrix as
622	  ``distance_field``: ``None`` for obstacles and for cells that cannot
623	  reach any endpoint, ``0`` for every endpoint, and otherwise the
624	  minimum over the endpoints of the accumulated entering-cell cost
625	  along a four-neighborhood route (unit steps without ``costs``; with
626	  ``costs`` each move adds the cost of the cell entered, the start
627	  cell's own cost never counted, exactly as ``plan``/``plan_any`` and
628	  ``distance_field`` accumulate). A reachable ``plan_any`` start yields
629	  the same value ``plan_any`` reports as ``cost``.
630	- ``targets`` is a matrix of the same shape: a reachable cell records
631	  the coordinate tuple of the endpoint that wins it, every other
632	  position is ``None`` (obstacles and unreachable cells, exactly where
633	  ``distances`` is ``None``); endpoints record themselves. When several
634	  endpoints tie at the same minimum distance the winner is the endpoint
635	  with the lexicographically smallest ``(x, y)`` coordinate, so the
636	  choice never depends on goal order. The whole result is
637	  JSON-serializable.
638	- ``expanded`` counts every reachable cell closed for the first time,
639	  all endpoints included, exactly once each. The closing order is
640	  smallest distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate
641	  lexicographically. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally
642	  carries ``expanded_nodes`` -- the coordinate pairs in that order,
643	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`` -- and the key is omitted
644	  entirely when ``trace`` is false or omitted.

1080	def _reservation_frames(paths):
1081	    # Compile normalized reservation paths into per-frame vertex and
1082	    # directed-edge sets. A path's t-th coordinate occupies its vertex at
1083	    # frame ``t``; past the final coordinate the last one persists, so
1084	    # the last compiled frame (index ``R - 1`` with ``R`` the longest
1085	    # path) doubles as the persistent tail, exactly like
1086	    # ``dynamic_blocked``'s last frame. Frame ``t``'s edge set holds the
1087	    # directed edges (p[t], p[t + 1]) of every path -- the move a
1088	    # candidate makes between frames ``t`` and ``t + 1`` may not traverse
1089	    # one of them in reverse. A stay or the persistent tail yields a
1090	    # self-edge, which never constrains a moving candidate (its vertex is
1091	    # reserved anyway).
1092	    horizon = max(len(path) for path in paths)
1093	    vertex_frames = []
1094	    edge_frames = []
1095	    for t in range(horizon):
1096	        vertices = set()
1097	        edges = set()
1098	        for path in paths:
1099	            current = path[t] if t < len(path) else path[-1]
1100	            nxt = path[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(path) else path[-1]
1101	            vertices.add(current)
1102	            edges.add((current, nxt))
1103	        vertex_frames.append(frozenset(vertices))
1104	        edge_frames.append(frozenset(edges))
1105	    return vertex_frames, edge_frames

1108	def _goal_not_before(paths, goal):
1109	    # The earliest frame at which a route may enter ``goal`` and then
1110	    # occupy it forever, given that every path in ``paths`` keeps its own
1111	    # final coordinate past its last frame: the frame after the last one
1112	    # in which any of ``paths`` occupies the cell. ``None`` when no path
1113	    # ever occupies it (no extra constraint); ``float("inf")`` when it is
1114	    # some path's final coordinate, whose occupancy persists, so no
1115	    # arrival can ever be safe.
1116	    latest = None
1117	    for path in paths:
1118	        if path[-1] == goal:
1119	            return float("inf")
1120	        for t in range(len(path) - 1, -1, -1):
1121	            if path[t] == goal:
1122	                if latest is None or t > latest:
1123	                    latest = t
1124	                break
1125	    return None if latest is None else latest + 1

1129	    # The last frame index a wait may enter: waits are only generated
1130	    # while the next time step still lies within the provided frames,
1131	    # where ``dynamic_blocked`` and ``reservations`` each provide frames
1132	    # (``None`` when neither does, which disables waiting).
1133	    last = None
1134	    if frames is not None:
1135	        last = len(frames) - 1
1136	    if vertex_frames is not None:

1311	def _search_static(width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, trace,
1312	                   max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False,
1313	                   allow_wait=False, state=None):
1314	    """Classic static-grid A* (the ``plan`` search without frames).
1315	
1316	    Cells are merged by coordinate: the best known ``g`` per cell is kept
1317	    in ``g_score``, stale heap entries are skipped, and ``came_from``
1318	    reconstructs the cheapest route once the goal is closed. With
1319	    ``max_cost`` a candidate whose accumulated entering-cell cost would
1320	    exceed the limit is discarded instead of queued, and the search
1321	    remembers whether any discard happened (``cost_limited``) so a
1322	    failure can be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of
1323	    the snapshot state so a resumed search stays equivalent to one
1324	    uninterrupted call. With
1325	    ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally returns a checkpoint of
1326	    the complete search state; ``state`` carries such a snapshot back in
1327	    so ``resume`` continues the identical traversal. The snapshot needs
1328	    the trace even when the caller did not ask for it, so nodes are
1329	    recorded whenever ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` is true.

1331	
1332	    def heuristic(point):
1333	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])

1335	    def step_cost(point):
1336	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
1337	        if costs is None:
1338	            return 1
1339	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
1340	
1341	    if state is None:
1342	        # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, point): the first four fields give
1343	        # a total, input-order-independent ordering, so the point itself
1344	        # is never compared.
1345	        h0 = heuristic(start)
1346	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], start)]
1347	        came_from = {}
1348	        g_score = {start: 0}
1349	        closed = set()
1350	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
1351	        cost_limited = False
1352	    else:
1353	        open_heap = state["open"]
1354	        came_from = state["came_from"]
1355	        g_score = state["g_score"]
1356	        closed = state["closed"]
1357	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
1358	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]
1359	    budget_stop = False
1360	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
1361	
1362	    while open_heap:
1363	        entry = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
1364	        current = entry[4]
1365	        if current in closed:
1366	            continue  # stale heap entry; already closed with its best g
1367	        if max_expanded is not None and len(closed) >= max_expanded:
1368	            # A live candidate remains but the budget is spent; close
1369	            # nothing more (this also covers start == goal with a zero
1370	            # budget: no node is closed and no start is fabricated). The
1371	            # popped candidate was already removed from the heap, so for a
1372	            # snapshot it is pushed back: the checkpoint must hold every
1373	            # still-live candidate for the search to resume exactly.
1374	            budget_stop = True
1375	            if snapshot:
1376	                heapq.heappush(open_heap, entry)
1377	            break

1379	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
1380	            expanded_nodes.append(current)
1381	        if current == goal:
1382	            path = [current]
1383	            while path[-1] in came_from:
1384	                path.append(came_from[path[-1]])
1385	            path.reverse()

1387	                "path": path,
1388	                "cost": g_score[current],
1389	                "expanded": len(closed),
1390	            }

1392	                result["status"] = "found"
1393	            if trace:
1394	                result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes

1396	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
1397	            nxt = (current[0] + dx, current[1] + dy)
1398	            if not (0 <= nxt[0] < width and 0 <= nxt[1] < height):
1399	                continue
1400	            if nxt in obstacles:
1401	                continue
1402	            new_g = g_score[current] + step_cost(nxt)
1403	            if new_g < g_score.get(nxt, float("inf")):
1404	                if max_cost is not None and new_g > max_cost:
1405	                    # The candidate's accumulated cost exceeds the limit:
1406	                    # discard it and remember that a discard happened.
1407	                    cost_limited = True
1408	                    continue
1409	                g_score[nxt] = new_g
1410	                came_from[nxt] = current
1411	                h = heuristic(nxt)
1412	                heapq.heappush(
1413	                    open_heap, (new_g + h, h, nxt[0], nxt[1], nxt)
1414	                )

1416	    if has_status:

1419	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
1420	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
1421	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
1422	            "plan", width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, None,
1423	            max_cost, len(closed), expanded_nodes,
1424	            _static_snapshot_state(open_heap, came_from, g_score, closed,
1425	                                   cost_limited, max_cost),
1426	            allow_wait,
1427	        )

1431	def _search_dynamic(width, height, obstacles, frames, start, goal, costs,
1432	                    trace, max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False,
1433	                    allow_wait=False, state=None, cost_frames=None,
1434	                    reservations=None, goal_not_before=None):
1435	    """History-sensitive time-expanded A*.
1436	
1437	    Frame ``t`` constrains the cell occupied at path index ``t``; frames
1438	    past the last one reuse the last frame. ``frames`` may be ``None``
1439	    when ``cost_frames`` or ``reservations`` is given: time-varying costs
1440	    or reserved routes alone already make the search space time-expanded.
1441	    With ``cost_frames`` the price of
1442	    entering a cell at time ``t`` is that frame's cell value (frames past
1443	    the last one reuse the last frame); the start cell is never counted.
1444	    With ``reservations`` (normalized reservation paths) a candidate
1445	    route may not enter a vertex another agent occupies at the same
1446	    frame, nor traverse the reverse of a reserved directed edge between
1447	    two frames; reserved vertices persist at each path's final
1448	    coordinate. Waiting in place (unless ``allow_wait`` is set) and repeated
1449	    coordinates are forbidden, so
1450	    whether a candidate route can be
1451	    extended depends on the exact sequence of cells it already visited:
1452	    two routes reaching the same ``(x, y, t)`` with different histories
1453	    are distinct states and neither may prune the other (the route with
1454	    the larger accumulated cost can be the only one that remains
1455	    extendable). Each heap node therefore carries its complete path; the
1456	    search is a best-first traversal of the feasible route tree. Goal
1457	    closings are collected until the heap's smallest f exceeds the best
1458	    goal cost, after which the minimum-cost goal tie-break is settled by
1459	    the fixed f, h, x, y, t priority and then the complete path's
1460	    lexicographic order. With ``max_cost`` a candidate route whose
1461	    accumulated entering-cell cost would exceed the limit is discarded
1462	    (``cost_limited`` records that any discard happened, so a failure can
1463	    be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of the snapshot
1464	    state). With ``allow_wait`` a route may also stay in its current cell
1465	    for one frame at no entering-cell cost, generated only while the next
1466	    time step still lies within the provided frames and the cell is free
1467	    there; consecutive waits repeat the coordinate in the path, and once
1468	    a cell is left it may never be re-entered. With ``goal_not_before``
1469	    (used by ``plan_agents``) a route may not enter the goal cell before
1470	    that frame, because a reserved route still occupies it at some later
1471	    frame and the goal cell stays occupied once the route ends; such
1472	    candidates are never generated, exactly like reserved vertices.
1473	    With ``snapshot=True`` a
1474	    budget stop additionally
1475	    returns a checkpoint of the complete route-tree state; ``state``
1476	    carries such a snapshot back in for ``resume``.
1477	    """
1478	
1479	    def heuristic(point):
1480	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
1481	
1482	    last_frame = len(frames) - 1 if frames is not None else None
1483	    last_cost_frame = len(cost_frames) - 1 if cost_frames is not None else None
1484	
1485	    def step_cost(point, t):
1486	        # Cost of entering ``point`` at time ``t``; the start cell is
1487	        # never entered. Time-varying frames take the value of frame
1488	        # ``t`` (the last frame persists); otherwise the static ``costs``
1489	        # matrix or unit steps apply.
1490	        if cost_frames is not None:
1491	            frame = (cost_frames[t] if t <= last_cost_frame
1492	                     else cost_frames[last_cost_frame])
1493	            return frame[point[1]][point[0]]
